units.why: "Given the advancements in artificial intelligence, be exceptionally clear!" tells instructors to state expectations about AI use and tools; the closest type is P09 (state AI expectations), though it is not tied to a syllabus.
units.fit_note: Does not say the statement must be in the syllabus; it says expectations about AI must be clear.

units.passage: The UCSB Writing Program suggests that instructors: “Communicate clear guidelines and expectations regarding the use of AI writing technology in the classroom, and transparency on which assignments and which parts of the writing process the use of AI writing tools may or may not be included, and the need for proper, clear, and continual attribution of any use of AI writing tools.”
units.why: The Writing Program is quoted: "Communicate clear guidelines and expectations regarding the use of AI writing technology". An instructor should state expectations, P09.

units.passage: Communicate expectations for student use of AI-writing assistive technologies in courses and/or other documents such as theses, dissertations, research articles, etc.
units.why: Item 1 is headed "Communicate expectations for student use of AI-writing assistive technologies", telling instructors to state expectations. That is P09 (state AI expectations), modality should since the memo calls it guidance.

units.passage: Consider including a policy statement specifically about the use of AI tools ( see examples in Sample Language for Syllabus Policies
units.why: "Consider including a policy statement specifically about the use of AI tools" asks instructors to put an AI statement in the syllabus, and points to sample language. P09 fits; modality should.

units.passage: Whether you incorporate generative AI use into your pedagogy or not, it’s important that you include a clear AI-use policy in your syllabus.
units.why: The guide says "it’s important that you include a clear AI-use policy in your syllabus", addressed to instructors, so it requires a syllabus statement (P09), not a stance.

units.passage: If you don’t, your students won’t know what is expected, what is allowed, and what is prohibited.
units.why: The sentence "your students won’t know what is expected, what is allowed, and what is prohibited" gives the consequence of omitting a syllabus AI policy, so it explains the instructor duty in the preceding sentence (before-course); it informs rather than directs, and fits P09.
units.fit_note: A: States the consequence of omitting a syllabus policy rather than the duty itself. B: Gives the reason for having a syllabus policy rather than the requirement itself.

units.passage: Address the following, drafting as clear and relevant a list as possible for each of the questions.
units.why: "Address the following, drafting as clear and relevant a list as possible" lists necessary components of a policy, so it asks instructors to cover specified questions in their syllabus policy (P09).
units.fit_note: Specifies the content of the policy, not only that one exists.

units.passage: If students are allowed to use AI, provide guidelines on appropriate vs. inappropriate use (e.g., using AI for idea generation vs. submitting AI-generated work as their own).
units.why: "provide guidelines on appropriate vs. inappropriate use" tells instructors who allow AI to state expectations for assignments, matching P09.

units.passage: Instructors should provide clear guidance for acceptable AI use.
units.why: "Instructors should provide clear guidance for acceptable AI use" asks instructors to state expectations, matching P09 (state AI expectations in syllabus/assignments), modality should.

units.passage: Including transparent language in the syllabus and assignment instructions specifying under what circumstances the use of AI/Tech tools is permitted is essential to student success.
units.policy: Instructors include transparent language in the syllabus and assignment instructions specifying under what circumstances the use of AI/Tech tools is permitted.
units.why: "Including transparent language in the syllabus and assignment instructions ... is essential" tells instructors to put the AI rule in the syllabus and assignments, P09.

units.passage: Under what circumstances AI use is permitted or forbidden
units.policy: Instructors consider stating in the syllabus under what circumstances AI use is permitted or forbidden.
units.why: Lists "Under what circumstances AI use is permitted or forbidden" as a consideration for syllabi: asks instructors to state expectations, P09.

units.passage: If you allow AI use in your course, remind students about the rules for AI use on every assignment.
units.why: "If you allow AI use in your course, remind students about the rules for AI use on every assignment" is a repeated-communication duty for instructors, P09.

units.passage: Be specific and let students know what class activities are permitted and not permitted for the use of generative AI tools.
units.why: Guidance tells instructors to be specific about permitted and not permitted class activities; 'Be specific and let students know' asks faculty to communicate expectations, so P09.

units.passage: Faculty should clearly define their AI usage policy in each course syllabus.
units.why: 'Faculty should clearly define their AI usage policy in each course syllabus' requires a syllabus AI statement, P09.

units.passage: Provide a statement in your syllabus:
units.why: 'Provide a statement in your syllabus' with specifics on permitted and not permitted activities, P09.

units.passage: Teach students about the current limitations of AI tools: AI doesn’t provide sources; use this as an opportunity to review how to properly cite research. AI can be inaccurate and even invent information. There are plenty of examples of AI getting the answer wrong; share amusing stories to illustrate this. AI can be used unethically. Fake news, deep fake videos. .. unfortunately, there are many examples. Teach students about the societal implications of AI: AI has the potential to shape the information we consume and the way we work and live....just like many other technological advances we have adapted to like the printing press and the internet! A great history lesson! Provide a statement in your syllabus: Be specific and let students know what class activities are permitted and not permitted for the use of generative AI tools.
units.why: The syllabus statement should 'Be specific and let students know what class activities are permitted and not permitted': P09; this page is coded on its own, so the repeat of the syllabus-statements wording is kept.

units.passage: and be sure to outline it explicitly in your Syllabus.
units.why: The same sentence continues "be sure to outline it explicitly in your Syllabus": instructors should put the AI rule in the syllabus. This is about where to communicate, so P09 (syllabus statement), not P04, which covers who decides.

units.passage: State your AI policies clearly on the syllabus
units.policy: State your AI policies clearly on the syllabus.
units.why: "State your AI policies clearly on the syllabus" tells instructors to put AI rules in the syllabus: should, P09.

units.passage: In the case of AI specifically, a complete policy would address:
units.policy: A complete AI policy addresses how students are permitted to use AI and what uses are explicitly forbidden.
units.why: "a complete policy would address" how students may use AI and which uses are forbidden, so an AI syllabus policy must state the rules: should, P09.

units.passage: Will the rules around AI vary from one assignment to the next? (If so, keep in mind that you’ll also need to write clear AI policies for any assignment that deviates from the general course policy)?
units.policy: Where AI rules vary from one assignment to the next, a clear AI policy is written for any assignment that deviates from the general course policy.
units.why: "you’ll also need to write clear AI policies for any assignment that deviates" requires assignment-level AI statements where rules differ: must, P09.

units.passage: Thus, you don’t need to address every possible tool, use, or contingency that might come up over the course of a term.
units.policy: A syllabus AI statement can be general and need not address every possible tool, use, or contingency.
units.why: "It’s okay to be a bit general when you frame these ideas" permits syllabus AI statements to be general: may, P09.

units.passage: That said, it’s probably best practice to include a more specific version of your AI policy as part of the prompt for every major writing assignment in your course.
units.policy: It is best practice to include a more specific version of the AI policy in the prompt for every major writing assignment.
units.why: "include a more specific version of your AI policy as part of the prompt" for every major writing assignment: should, P09.

units.passage: When AI use is permissible, it will be clearly stated in the assignment prompt posted in Canvas
units.why: "When AI use is permissible, it will be clearly stated in the assignment prompt posted in Canvas" commits the instructor to state expectations in assignment instructions, P09.
